studies.title: Reproducible Benchmarking Platform for Networked Control Systems
studies.evidence: The wiki links this full-text study specifically to the sample files. Grouped with the main benchmarking study, not counted as an additional publication.

measurement_semantics: Single published wireless example, not an industrial PLC, a set of independent repeats, or multi-robot scheduling. Robot code uses a physical LEGO platform gyro and encoders, the remote controller calculates actuation and UDP carries both directions.

Robot.py lines 234–255: tsr immediately precedes gyro and encoder reads; tsstx precedes send_sensor_signals. Report k+1 carries robot times for k but the current sensor readings. The motor_voltage_applied fields report the values held in the software, not a terminal measurement.

Lines 285–316: regular receive branch checks command sequence against the current cycle, schedules application around the next trigger and records taw after both SetDuty calls. Lines 89–109: motor setpoints are converted to rounded, clipped percentage duty and written/flushed to sysfs. An instantaneous measured voltage, GPIO edge and first physical motion are absent.

Lines 340–356: local-prediction fallback synthesizes a theoretical receive marker and stamps its local write; no unambiguous fallback flag is in the timing CSVs. Passage of the voltage consistency filter is not proof of packet delivery or causality. No independently synchronized one-way delay or absolute information age is inferred.

Distinct timing domains: six intervals use separate differences within the robot monotonic clock, controller monotonic clock, or the capture clock. The robot read-to-post-write interval includes scheduled waiting. Wire/hardware receive/transmit instants are not measured by the application markers.
file_checks: Six 1,684-row telemetry streams match corresponding integer sensor payload fields for all 1,684 logged rows, including recorded motor setpoint telemetry. Six 1,389-row timing streams match the four 100 ns robot fields exactly; the host receive stamp matches telemetry at k and host pre-send stamp is within one 100 ns encoding tick of the transmitted command.

Joined robot cycles 295..1683 use reports 296..1684. Capture shows one further control repeat/window k=1684 outside the timing CSV coverage; sensor captures extend to 1746. The capture ends in one incomplete unrelated UDP record; the two experiment-port payload families were complete. No clock or sample ordering is extrapolated outside the joined window.

1,333 applied/commanded pairs agree exactly in integer microvolt encodings; 1,385 pairs agree within one unit at both sides; four disagree by over one. Compare both populations in the timing summary. No packet fault or new applied command is imputed. The controller lost counter counts observed sequence gaps, which differs from proof of end-to-end delivery.

The precomputed controller processing/robot round-trip CSVs have only headers. All intervals in this release were independently reconstructed from data-bearing files. Quantiles use linear interpolation.
reproduce: python derive_ncsbench.py <NCSbench checkout>/benchmark/measurements/platform-a-wireless <output-directory> (Python 3, NumPy). Read local source files only. Source-file lengths and SHA-256 digests are in ncsbench-source-files.csv.
